| `1` | Command ran but reported a failu

## Use from an MCP client instead of a shell

If your agent spe
aks MCP but can't run shell commands (Claude Desktop, chat clients), run the same testing engine as a stdio MCP server:\n\n```bash

theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
npx -y @mcpjam/cli@latest mcp
```

Connections to servers under test stay open between to
ol calls, so agents can also observe notifications and session behavior that one-shot CLI commands can't. See [MCPJam as an MCP se

rver](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/mcp-server.md).

# MCPJam API

> Pro
grammatic access to the MCP servers in your MCPJam projects — diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval run

s.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview.** It works today and we use it ourselves, but
> it has not been generall
y announced and the surface may change — including in\n> breaking ways — while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n
> behaviors documented on this page, build a [tolerant\n> reader](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is v

ery
> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or
> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card]
[Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)\n>\n> Go straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're si

gned out,
> you'll be asked to sign in and then land right back on the API keys page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP
servers saved in your\n[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) projects — from CI, scripts, or your own agents —\nwit

hout opening the UI.

What you can do with it today:

* **Discover your resources** — list your projects, their servers, eval\
n suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the other routes need is\n self-serve\n* **Validate a server** — connect, initialize, a
nd capture a capability snapshot\n* **Run the doctor** — the probe → connect → initialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth
requirements** — does this server need an OAuth grant?\n* **List tools, prompts, and resources** — the server's MCP primitives\n*
**Call a tool / render a prompt** — execute primitives and get the MCP result back verbatim\n* **Read a resource** by URI\n* **Ex
port a full snapshot** — tools, resources, and prompts as one JSON document\n* **Manage a project's clients** — list, read, **crea
te** (from a built-in\n template like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a full config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the nam
ed, reusable configurations that define how\n MCPJam connects to and talks to your MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n rea
d the client, then send its `configId` back as `expectedConfigId` for a\n config change and its `name` back as `expectedName` for
a rename — a rename\n does not rotate the config, so the config token cannot detect a concurrent\n one — and a concurrent edit
is rejected rather than silently reverted\n* **Manage a project's environments** — list, read, create, edit, archive, and\n resto
re the named execution bundles (host + optional server group + optional\n pinned skills and plugin versions) that eval suites and
goals run against,\n and **preview** what one resolves to before launching it\n* **List a project's studies** — name, access mod
e, attached servers, and\n share link — and **read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,\n tool-approval policy, and res
olved servers\n* **Author eval suites** — create a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, test cases) synchronously and get
a `suiteId` back; no run is started and no credits are spent\n* **Run eval suites asynchronously** — create a run from a saved su
ite, get a `202` + `runId`\n immediately, then poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, token\n usage, latency), and full
traces. Runs appear live in the hosted UI,\n tagged `source: \"api\"`\n* **Manage a server's accounts** — complete OAuth yoursel
f (e.g. the SDK's\n `runOAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n account; list, rename, choose t
he default, and delete accounts. Tokens are\n write-only: no route returns one\n* **Run a headless agent turn** — send a message
history, get back the\n assistant reply, the platform operations it invoked, references to any\n resources it created (eval suit
es), and token usage; the model is pinned\n server-side and billed to the project\n* **Send feedback** — report a bug, a missing
capability, or something\n confusing to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the\n `send_feedback` MCP to

ol calls

All endpoints operate on servers you have already added to a project in the
hosted inspector. Managing API keys remai

ns UI-only — see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https:

//app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.

## Auth

entication

Every request needs an MCPJam API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}\
ncurl -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bear

er $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings →
API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)\n in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there\n
